description: Three hooks. (1) PreToolUse on ExitPlanMode — Plan Briefing checkpoint: a deterministic, stateless Node command hook on EVERY ExitPlanMode (Quick Fix Mode, /create-spec & /update-spec plan phases, and plain plan mode). It allows when a real user reply precedes the call — skipping the agent's mechanical tool turns (e.g. the ToolSearch that loads a deferred ExitPlanMode, a post-approval Edit) so they do not break the check — and blocks a straight planning -> ExitPlanMode skip with a short reminder. The check is anchored to the current plan session: a first pass finds where plan mode was (re-)entered — an EnterPlanMode tool call, or a genuine transition into plan read from a real user message's own permissionMode field (the reliable signal for a manual shift+tab re-entry after a restart drops plan-mode state) — then a second pass walks back only to that boundary, so a deny never points at stale text from a previous plan session or from before a restart. Crucially, a bare permission-mode:plan marker seen WHILE ALREADY in plan is ignored, not treated as a boundary: Claude Code writes one at essentially every plan-mode turn boundary, and the old logic mistook those for a fresh re-entry and false-blocked the compliant briefed-then-replied flow whenever a routine marker sat between the reply and the exit. Fail-open on any uncertainty, so it never deadlocks. Filters subagent (isSidechain) and injected (isMeta) entries. Reads the transcript only; writes nothing anywhere. (2) SessionStart on startup/resume — injects a short reminder (session-start-skill-reminder.js) to load and use the spec-driven-development skill for any code work. Static context injection, no project detection: the reminder itself states the 'if this is a code project' condition and lets the agent judge. Writes nothing. (3) PreToolUse on SendMessage - executor context checkpoint: a subagent is resumed by messaging it, so this is the one moment a hook can put a fact in front of the resume decision. It resolves the target agent id to that subagent's own transcript, reads the tail for the last usage record, and treats cache_read + cache_creation + input as the session's current context size. At 300K it notes that the ceiling is near; from 400K it says the session should be retired. It emits additionalContext and nothing else - no permissionDecision on either band - so the call always passes through untouched and the hook can never block, prompt, or alter it. THE AXIS CHANGED IN 1.22.0: the first version counted resumes and spoke at #15/#25. That worked in the narrow sense (the 105- and 119-resume tail vanished within a day) but measured the wrong thing - cost and defocus track context size, not resume count, and bounded dispatches continued by resume are the prescribed shape, so the old axis would have fired on exactly the behaviour the skill now asks for. Executors were measured at a median peak of 461K and as high as 997K, with 151 compact_boundary markers across the subagent transcripts: past that the harness autocompacts the executor, which then works from a lossy summary of its design basis. 400K is enforced by RETIREMENT, not compaction - it sits far below the ~930K compaction point, so a session retired on time is never compacted, and a fresh spawn re-reads the authoritative docs from disk while a compacted session keeps only a paraphrase. Complements the maxTurns ceilings in the agent frontmatter, which bound one dispatch (invisible to this hook, since no SendMessage happens mid-dispatch) while this bounds accumulation across dispatches (invisible to maxTurns, whose budget resets on every resume). Deliberately not a gate: whether the session holds tacit knowledge a fresh spawn would lose is visible only to the main agent. Reviewer sessions are not exempt. Fail-open on everything - a `to` that is not a subagent id (a peer session or teammate name), an absent or unreadable subagent transcript, a parse error, or no usage record yet. Reads stdin + transcripts only (tail only); writes nothing.
